Specific details of planned events have not been confirmed, but are likely to occur in major cities across the country. Previous climate strikes have seen large turnout in cities such as New York City, Philadelphia, and Washington, D.C.

Available images show a large billboard collapsed against the Flyover Rainbow Antapani causing significant congestion on Jalan Terusan Jakarta. There are no reports of casualties at this time. Travellers in Bandung should drive with caution and be prepared to alter routes at short notice. Keep abreast of the latest weather forecasts and defer journeys if necessary.

Risk analysis: Striking taxi drivers launched protests on 23 January to demand the regulation of services offered by ride-sharing providers such as Uber and Cabify. On 29 January, their representatives warned that the protests would continue indefinitely until a deal was reached with the authorities. Hundreds of taxi drivers are likely to gather in several areas of central Madrid, including Gran Via, Puerta del Sol, and Calle de Genova outside the People's Party's (Partido Popular: PP) headquarters, to block traffic, causing severe road cargo and transport disruption. Osaka’s G20 summit likely to impede logistics operations from June 27-30 Japan will host its first ever Group of Twenty (G20) summit at Osaka’s International Exhibition Center on June 28-29, 2019. The G20 summit is held annually for governments of 20 member nations to discuss a wide range of issues affecting the world’s economy. In light of the high profile event, Japanese authorities have released a statement detailing large-scale traffic and sea restrictions near Osaka Port, Kansai International Airport (KIX), as well as within Osaka city during the summit period. As KIX is the country’s third largest airport and a key logistics hub for engineering and automotive companies from southern and central regions of Japan, heightened security checks and restrictions may significantly affect cargo handling and delivery for industries that rely heavily on this route. 

Organizers of the G20 summit reportedly aim to reduce traffic by 50 percent for four days, during and leading up to the event. To this end, local authorities have set up traffic restrictions in and around Osaka especially for roads connecting to KIX. The airport is built on an artificial island in Osaka Bay; thus the bridge that connects KIX to Rinku town on the main island will be the most impacted route, particularly on June 27 and June 30 during the arrival and departure of head of states. 

From June 27-30, 10 major sections of Hanshin Expressway including No.1 Loop Route and the Gulf Line totaling about 160 kilometers that connects to KIX, hotels, and the summit venue will be closed to traffic from morning until late evening to facilitate movement of delegates and participants of the summit. As a result, traffic will likely be diverted to other expressways such as Meishin Expressway. In Osaka, traffic restrictions will be in effect at 9 locations: Osaka Station, Nakanoshima, Tenma, Osaka Castle, Honcho, Uehoncho, Namba, Tennoji, and Nanko. 

In order to access international cargo and fuel supply areas, authorities have set up a fixed route bus that goes from Kansai Airport Station to these areas. However, the bus may not operate normally due to traffic restrictions and logistics providers have been advised to allow for extra travel time. 

According to official statements by the local authorities, heightened security checks can be expected at three main entry points in Kansai region: Kansai International Airport, Osaka International Airport (also known as Itami Airport), and Kobe Airport. Due to their proximity to the event venue, Kansai and Osaka Airports will be used widely by the participants and both airports have released statements pertaining to cargo inspections. 

While no airlines have publicly announced additional flights during the aforementioned period, both airports have pre-warned about possible flight delays on June 27 and June 30 due to the arrival and departure of aircrafts carrying heads of states and government officials. Both airports also have prohibited flying drones above and around the facilities; KIX in particular has restricted flying drones within 1,000 meters of the airport. 

According to the statement released by authorities, all vessels entering the sea near Osaka Port and KIX from June 24–30 are requested to provide prior notification to Japan’s maritime security department by noon at least the day before the planned navigation date. Failure to do so would result in longer berthing times. Shipping companies can submit earlier notifications to the nearest maritime security department starting from June 3–19. In addition, vessels are also requested to refrain from entering designated restricted areas, referred to as ""voluntary navigation restraint sea area"", around the airport island and the ""exclusive use sea area"" between the two parts of the island.

Traffic restrictions in and out of KIX for 4-days are likely to be the main challenge for Everstream Analytics customers with airfreight as collection service for KIX from major domestic shipping companies and delivery service centered in Osaka are likely to be disrupted, particularly on June 27 and 30. In addition to road restrictions, security spot checks on vehicles and cargo inspections may take longer than usual prior to and during the summit.

It is possible that local freight forwarders may pick up imported air cargo arriving during the G20 summit period from July 1 onwards. Thus, customers are advised to liaise with local contacts to avoid delays for critical cargo, such as perishable or pharmaceutical goods, that may require special handling. Alternatively, customers can also consider rerouting shipments to Tokyo’s Narita Airport to avoid delays. This option was used by manufacturers when KIX was shut down for 3-days due to the destruction caused by Typhoon Jebi in 2018.

UPDATE: Up to 11 vessels waiting for a berth at Port of Qingdao Updated sources on October 11 indicate that there were 4 vessels waiting for a berth at Qingdao Qianwan Container Terminal (QQCT), 2 vessels waiting for a berth at Qingdao Qianwan United Container Terminal (QQCTU) and 1 vessel waiting for a berth at QQCTN terminals.

Port congestion reported at Port of Dammam due to reduced staff Shipping sources on April 3 report that the Saudi Arabian port of Dammam is facing congestion due to reduced turnaround of staff as the government imposed COVID-19 related quarantines.

UPDATE - USA, Virginia: Tropical Storm Michael results in fatalities, power outages, and road closures overnight in Virginia Media sources are confirming at least five storm-related fatalities in Virginia as a result of Tropical Storm Michael overnight. As of this morning, the Virginia Department of Emergency Management released statistics confirming the fatalities as well as indicating that around 520,000 are without power and nearly 1,200 roadways are closed due to flooding and downed trees. Emergency officials are urging motorists to take extra precautions if transiting the area. A Flood Warning remains in effect in the eastern region of Virginia until 10:45 EDT. Travelers are advised to actively monitor weather and media outlets for situational updates. Motorists should keep apprised of ongoing road closures via traffic reports and avoid areas where flood conditions persist.

Strong winds to disrupt port operations across South Africa until December 23 Shipping sources indicate on December 21 that severe weather is likely to impact operations at container terminals in South Africa between November December 19 and 23, in particular in the Port of Durban, the Port of Coega and the Port of Cape Town. As a result, productivity is likely to be reuced and incoming vessels may be delayed.

Cargo vessel skips Port Klang for schedule recovery Intelligence received by Everstream Analytics indicated on December 2 that PS3 Service Vessel ONE COMPETENCE 0076E was due to arrive at Port of Nhava Sheva on December 11 and at Port of Pipava in India on December 14. The vessel is expected to skip Port Klang in Malaysia for schedule recovery.

In Mongla, Bagerhat, Bangladesh Coast Guard personnel seized a trawler and In Mongla, Bagerhat, Bangladesh Coast Guard personnel seized a trawler and arrested 16 Indian fishermen from Fairway Boya in the Bay of Bengal for fishing illegally in its waters.

UPDATE: Situation at Port of Ningbo back to normal following congestion Updated sources on August 22 indicate that the situation at Ningbo Port has been back to normal. Previously, sources reported that XiaZhi channel leading into the Port of Ningbo-Zhoushan has been closed on August 22 for about 5 hours, due to the congestion of fishing boats with average waiting times for vessels calling at the port reported 10 hours.

Authorities allowed ships loaded with cargo to berth Industry sources reported that Kuwait’s Ministry of Health recommends allowing ships carrying goods from the Republic of Korea, Italy, Thailand, Singapore, Japan, China and Hong Kong to berth. The circular was released on February 26 and the emphasis remains on prohibiting direct contact with the crew and preventing them from disembarking from the ship for two weeks from the date of their departure from the affected ports.

UPDATE: Delays reported in the Port of Rotterdam due to bad weather effects On December 10, updated reports suggest that knock-on effects from adverse weather in the Port of Rotterdam on the past weekend have caused a pilot and tug boat shortages as well as heavy incoming ship traffic. As a result, vessels have been delayed at berth as well as on departure times. Customers should plan shipments and use contingency measures accordingly.

Cargo ship drags anchor during typhoon, colliding with bridge in Yokohama Sources indicate that on September 9 at 03:10 local time, the cargo ship ""Bungo Princess"" (IMO 9496654) dragged its anchor and collided with the harbor road bridge in Yokohama under typhoon conditions. Damages to the vessel are not known. The vessel was able to navigate under its own power away from the area.

Severe winds impact operations at Pier 1 Container Terminal, Port of Durban Industry sources indicated that Pier 1 Container Terminal at the Port of Duran has experienced a temporary suspension due to severe winds for its waterside and landside operations at 16:25 (local time) on September 12. It remains unclear when the operations will resume.

Rua Jo o Negr o & Rua Alfredo Bufren   Striking teachers left after protesting. Incident closed. Media sources reported that up to 2,500 teachers held a protest at Pra a Santos Andrade, located at Rua Jo o Negr o and Rua Alfredo Bufren. Teachers have since dispersed after demonstrating. Local news outlets indicated that multiple roads were closed. The demonstration was called to support an ongoing teachers  strike, and to commemorate the 30th anniversary of a teachers  strike that was held in 1988. Expect possible residual protest-related disruptions. This incident is closed.

Extreme morning traffic congestion near Port of Genoa disrupting operations Sources indicate that extensive roadway construction on the Autostradale to the north and west of the Port of Genoa has resulted in extreme traffic congestion and port disruptions in the mornings and some late evenings. Reports suggest that the construction, which is scheduled to run from 22:00 to 06:00, is sometimes running over schedule into the mornings. Resulting from traffic congestion, some reports indicate that police have been able to assist the port such that approximately 5 trucks per 5 minutes are able to leave the area, but this support has been inconsistent. At times, port gates have reportedly been completely blocked. Supply chain managers should anticipate significant cargo transportation disruptions entering and exiting the port during the morning and late evening times as a result.

Adverse weather disrupts cargo movements in Valencia area Shipping sources on January 20 indicate that heavy rainfall and flooding has impacted ground transportation movements in the greater Valencia area. Many roads remain blocked and shipment delays should be anticipated.

UPDATE 1 - Terminal congestion reported at Port of Busan following Tropical Storm Jangmi Updated shipping sources indicated on August 13 that the Port of Busan terminal is experiencing congestion due to Tropical Storm Jangmi, which closed the port from August 10 00:01 to August 10 19:00 local time. Pilotage resumed on August 11 00:01 local time.

Port of Kandla hoists Signal No. 1 ahead of cyclonic storm According to industry sources, all ports along the coast from Gujarat including the Port of Kandla (Gujarat), Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust, Mumbai Port in Maharashtra and Mormugao Port in Goa have hoisted Distant Cautionary Signal No. 1 (DC-I) ahead of a cyclonic storm in the Arabian Sea.

Update: Tropical Storm Warning in effect for South Carolina Updated sources indicate that the Hurricane Warning from Savannah River to south of Edisto Beach, South Carolina has been changed to a Tropical Storm Warning. A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are expected within the warning area within 36 hours.

Mexico: Tropical Storm Xavier forms off coastline of Colima State The National Hurricane Center is monitoring Tropical Storm Xavier off the western coastline of Colima State on Saturday, 3 November. The storm is not expected to make landfall at this time and is forecast to move in a northwest direction early next week; however, some rainfall may be experienced near the coastal areas of Colima and Jalisco states. Currently, the system is located about 600 kilometers southwest of Manzanillo, with wind speeds up to 75 kmh and moving east-northeast at 11 kmh. There are no weather warnings in effect this morning. Clients are advised to monitor weather reports for the latest information. Amend itineraries as necessary if the storm's path changes.

Houston Ship Channel closes for four hours due to salvage operations Industry sources indicate that the Houston Ship Channel will be closed between 08:00 and 12:00 local time on January 24 due to salvage operations from Galveston Bay Entrance Channel lighted buoys 9 and 10 out to Galveston North and South Jetty lights 5A and 6A.

Pipeline removal to cause mild disruption in Houston VTS Channel Industry sources indicate on July 15 that removal of a submerged dredge pipeline between LT Buoy 102A to LT Buoy 103 below Fred Hartman La Port will result in mild maritime disruptions in the vicinity at the Port of Houston.

UPDATE 7 - Average waiting times at the Port of Jakarta continue to stand at 2 days Updated shipping sources indicate on May 20 that waiting times at the Port of Jakarta, Indonesia, continue to stand at 2 days. There was no change from the previous weeks.

Strict customs inspections cause customs delays at Port of Xiamen Shipping sources report on December 10 that strict customs inspections and disinfection requirements for reefers imports to Port of Xiamen have caused customs delays. As a result, inbound reefer container pick-up activity at the Ports of Xiamen in southern China has been slow and is facing congestion. International shipping lanes like Ocean Network Express have stopped accepting bookings of all reefer booking commodities bound for Xiamen effectively from December 9.

U.S. chicken shipments bound for China rerouted due to coronavirus Media sources indicate on February 14 that ships carrying refrigerated cargo containers of U.S. chicken shipments bound for China are being diverted to ports in Hong Kong, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam due to the coronavirus outbreak. Chinese ports have reportedly run out of space for refrigerated containers and must be plugged into electrical outlets once they are offloaded to keep frozen meat and other food products cold.

Inbound river vessel traffic to and from Port of Hamburg suspended due to Storm Ciara Shipping sources report that the inbound river to and from the Port of Hamburg has been closed since 07:00 local time on February 9 for vessels longer than 330 meters. This ban could be extended until Wednesday, February 12. Terminal operations are reportedly working.

Reports of strike action at Civil Hospital in Karachi Unconfirmed reports have stated that the 'Young Doctors of Civil Hospital' are striking at the hospital in Karachi today. They are doing so against the hospital administration and disruption has been noted to services provided to patients. Further details have not been disclosed at this time.

UPDATE - USA, California: State of Emergency declared for portions of Ventura and Los Angeles counties impacted by wildfires Acting Governor Newsom has declared a State of Emergency for portions Ventura and Los Angeles counties on Friday, 9 November, due to the growing Woolsey and Hill wildfires. This will direct further resources to the impacted localities to aid in the firefighting operations. Evacuation orders remain in effect for residents north and south of the Ventura Freeway, between Camarillo, Calabasas, and Malibu. Notable congestion continues to be recorded near the Ventura Freeway and the Pacific Coast Highway as closures are in place, authorities are directing traffic, and evacuations are ongoing. A Red Flag Warning is in place through Friday evening across Ventura and Los Angeles counties, with dry conditions and wind gusts making firefighting efforts challenging. Clients are advised to avoid all impacted areas and terrain, as the fires remain uncontained and hazardous. Refer to official and media sources for the latest information on the situation. Adhere to all instructions issued by local authorities.

Severe wind warning issued across country A severe wind warning is in effect across Malta until 23:59 local time on Monday 23 December. Gusts of up to 75 kilometres per hour are anticipated in Valletta and other areas. There could be delays to public transport, power cuts and damage to properties.
Port of Charleston - The port has resumed normal operations. Incident closed. The Port of Charleston has resumed normal operations following the passage of Hurricane Dorian. This incident is closed.

Reefer yard remains full at Port of Chittagong Industry sources report on October 7 that the reefer yard remains full at Port of Chittagong. Terminals are under severe berth congestion with low productivity. The waiting time is likely to be around 1 to 2 days.
Port operations normal at Port Klang Media sources reported that the port operations are generally normal at Port Klang. WP terminal is tight in reefer plugs availability with some restrictions.

30 miles W of San Antonio de los Cobres - A magnitude 4.0 earthquake has been reported in the area. Event closed. - UPDATE 1 The European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre is reporting a magnitude 4.0 earthquake located 30 miles west of San Antonio de los Cobres, Argentina. EMSC (European Mediterranean Seismological Centre) is a scientific international organization, which aggregates and provides information generated by national seismological agencies worldwide. EMSC presents earthquake data across several magnitude scales including local magnitude (ML), surface-wave magnitude (Ms), body-wave magnitude (Mb), and moment magnitude (Mw). All magnitude scales should yield approximately the same value for any given earthquake.

Qinzhou port bans logistics companies until February 9 Media sources indicate on February 6 that the Qinzhou port has banned local logistics companies from operating until February 9 in an effort to contain the coronavirus outbreak. Truck delivery is also affected by strict road restrictions there. The temporary closure has inhibited alloy smelters outside the port area from transporting ore to their plants.

Operations suspended at Dammam Port Industry sources reported that the Dammam Port Marine operations were temporarily suspended at 13:12 hours local time today, October 22, due to strong wind and rain. For safety reasons, the Port Authority/marine department halted ships’ movement for docking/undocking during high wind speed.

Anti-drug agents in Rotterdam port, Netherlands, seized over a ton of cocaine Anti-drug agents in Rotterdam port, Netherlands, seized over a ton of cocaine in a container loaded with bananas that had departed from Guayaquil.

Average waiting times of 12 hours reported at Port of Yangshan Shipping sources on May 7 indicate that average waiting times of 12 hours are currently occurring at the Shanghai Guandong Container Terminal in the Port of Yangshan.

UPDATE 4 - United Kingdom—RMT members on Caledonian Sleeper trains staged strikes on Sun and Mon. Event closed. Updated sources report that Rail, Maritime and Transport Union (RMT) members who work on Caledonian Sleeper trains were on strike again on Sunday, October 11, and Monday, October 12. All Caledonian Sleeper Highland services, which runs from London Euston to Fort William, were canceled on October 11 and October 12. Caledonian Sleeper Lowland services, which runs from London Euston to Edinburgh, will run with a reduced schedule on October 11 and October 12.

All Caledonian Sleeper services were canceled on Sunday, October 4, and Monday, October 5, due to a two-day strike by Rail, Maritime and Transport Union (RMT) members. The strike was called due to concerns with the safety and well-being of transportation workers. Commuters are encouraged to contact the rail service regarding travel specific information. This event is closed.

UPDATE 2 - Alexandria Port Authority announces closure of Alexandria Port inlet Updated Arabic-language media sources indicate on January 8 that Alexandria Port Authority has announced the closure of Alexandria Port inlet, starting at 15:30 on January 6 due to severe weather. Inlet closure is reportedly continuing on January 8, it is unclear when operations would resume. According to sources, loading and unloading operations and movement of goods and trucks are running as usual.

Japan: Hokuriku Shinkansen services remain suspended due to impact of Typhoon Hagibis Japanese reports have confirmed that Hokuriku Shinkansen services in Tokyo remain suspended due to the impact of Typhoon Hagibis over the weekend. The full resumption of the service is estimated in one to two weeks. The typhoon had flooded the bullet train depot in Nagano City and damaged a large number of cars and the electrical equipment is reported to have been damaged.  The operator has confirmed they will only be able to operate at 50 to 60 percent capacity, even after service is resumed for the entire line between Tokyo and Kanazawa.

Strong winds likely to suspend operations at the Port of Kobe Local sources on August 21 report that there is a high potential for intermittent closures of the Port of Kobe, Japan, due to strong winds in the afternoon of August 22. The closure may last 48 hours and is likely to cause moderate congestion due to container backlogs. Customers with an interest in shipping in the port should activate short-term contingency measures.

UPDATE 11 - Severe berth congestion continues at Port of Chittagong Updated sources indicate on June 17 that severe berth congestion due to low productivity continues to be reported at the Port of Chittagong. Waiting times of up to 6 1/2 days have been reported for ships calling at the port.

Los Angeles County & Orange County - Uber & Lyft drivers embarked on 1 day strike. Incident closed. Uber and Lyft drivers associated with Rideshare Drivers United embarked on a one-day strike across Los Angeles County and Orange County. The labor action was organized to protest a 25 percent wage cut and to urge Uber to pay drivers at least $28 an hour. Drivers picketed outside the Uber Greenlight Hub in Redondo Beach, but have since left the area. This incident is closed.

Port operations suspended at Port of Dalian due to strong wind from Nov 18-19 Shipping sources on November 20 report that port operations were suspended at Port of Dalian from November 18 early morning until November 19 early morning. This was reportedly due to strong winds in the area. Increased waiting times in the coming days are likely.

Port of Osaka may be disrupted due to strong winds on March 15 Shipping sources indicate on March 13 that strong winds are likely to cause the port closure of the Port of Osaka on March 16 (morning to evening). Customers should anticipate delays.

UPDATE: Port of Tokyo suspends all operations on October 11 Updated media sources indicate on October 11 that the Port of Tokyo has suspended all operations for today. Sources stated that operations at all Japanese ports is expected to resume on October 13 in the afternoon or October 14 dawn based on the weather forecast.

Employee engagement session may disrupt operations at Port of Durban On October 23, industry sources report that Durban MPT will be hosting an engagement session with all employees at the Port of Durban, South Africa, from 10:30 local time on October 23. Delays to waterside and landside operations should be expected for the duration of the session.

Workers with Ertsoverslagbedrijf Europoort C.V. (EECV) threaten to go on strike at the Port of Rotterdam On November 17, Dutch media sources reported that workers with Ertsoverslagbedrijf Europoort C.V. (EECV) threaten to go on strike at the Port of Rotterdam. The strike will reportedly take place if EECV does not agree to a better collective agreement in the coming days, but no specific strike date was announced yet. EECV handles bulk cargo at the Port of Rotterdam.

UPDATE 1 - High yard density continues to disrupt operations at Port of Antwerp Shipping sources indicate on November 19 that high yard density continues to be reported at the Port of Antwerp. According to sources, an overflow of imports from UK ports that were not discharged due to the congestion situation there is likely to disrupt operations in Antwerp, with limited flexibility and possible affect on port stays and limited berthing possibilities.

Congestion reported at Virginia International Gateway due to wind disurptions Shipping sources indicate on November 4 that congestion has been reported at Virginia International Gateway in Portsmouth, Virginia. According to sources, the congestion is due to wind disruptions.

UPDATE 6 - Phillips 66 to begin restart of Lake Charles refinery by end of week following infrastructure damage Updated sources indicate on October 13 that Phillips 66 is to begin to restart the Lake Charles refinery by the end of this week, according to company representatives. Previously, the Phillips 66 Lake Charles Manufacturing Complex, Gulf Coast Lubricants Plant and Lake Charles area terminals and pipelines experienced only minimal damages in the passage of Hurricane Delta. The refinery was previously shut since August 25 due to extensive damage to the electrical power infrastructure by Hurricane Laura. The Phillips 66 Company is an American multinational energy company headquartered in Westchase, Houston, TX.

8 miles SW of Manzanillo - A magnitude 4.7 earthquake was reported in the area. Incident closed. The U.S. Geological Survey reported a magnitude 4.7 earthquake located approximately eight miles southwest of Manzanillo, Mexico in the Pacific Ocean. There were no initial reports of injuries or major structural damage. This incident is closed.

London - Central and Waterloo & City lines held a 24-hour strike on November 7. Incident closed. Train drivers with the RMT and Aslef unions on the Central and Waterloo & City Lines of the London Underground held a 24-hour strike today, November 7. The strike was held as part of a series of labor actions over disagreements with management. Service on the two lines will resume a normal schedule on November 8. This incident is closed.

Port of Taichung to close between Jan 24-26 for Lunar New Year Industry sources reported that Port of Keelung will be closed from 12.00 local time on January 24 until 08.00 of January 26 due to the Lunar New Year.

Inbound channels closed at Port of Ningbo due to dense fog Shipping sources on July 9 indicate that Xiazhimen and Tiaozhoumen inbound channels at the Port of Ningbo have been closed from July 8 afternoon due to dense fog. No estimation as to when the situation will improve was immediately provided.

Port operations suspended at Zhoushan due to Hagupit Local media sources indicate on August 5 that port operations halted at the Port of Zhoushan due to the arrival of Hagupit on August 5. The suspension is anticipated to last through August 8, and is anticipated to adversely impact the trade of 25,000 tons of bunker fuel.

UPDATE 3 - Germany - Deutsche Post and the Verdi union reached an agreement for a wage increase. Event closed. Media sources reported that Deutsche Post and the Verdi union have reached an agreement after a strike in Germany that began on Friday, September 18 in states across the country. Nearly 140,000 collective bargaining employees with Deutsche Post will be impacted by the increase. The parties agreed to a deal that provides for wage increases in two stages until 2022. Apprentices with the union will also apparently receive a wage increase. Sources indicated that in the past two weeks, upwards of 22,000 workers at more than 300 locations throughout Germany took part in warning strikes on a total of six days. The following regions were impacted by the strike in mail delivery and municipal services: Berlin and Brandenburg, Baden-Wurttemberg, Bavaria, Hamburg, Hessen, Lower Saxony and Bremen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Rhineland-Palatinate and Saarland, Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt, Thuringia, Schleswig-Holstein, and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. There are no reports of residual disruptions, although they are possible. This event is closed.

At Jakarta Container Terminal, duty oiler, on routine rounds, onboard a... At Jakarta Container Terminal, duty oiler, on routine rounds, onboard a berthed containership, spotted two robbers in the engine room and immediately raised the alarm; seeing an alerted crew the robbers fled empty-handed.

South Africa: Demonstration by striking taxi drivers causing disruption along John Ross Highway near Richards Bay It has been reported that John Ross Highway has been blocked near Richards Bay by protesting taxi drivers that are participating in the strike action. The road is blocked between Meerensee to Empangeni. The reason for the demonstration is unclear; however there is a possibility for unrest. Drivers are urged to use alternative routes in the area.

Flooding impacts operations at Port of Santos Local sources report on February 5 that heavy rainfall flooding is currently impacting multiple neighborhoods across Sao Paulo. Roads have been flooded and traffic from and to port terminals at the Port of Santos has been severely impeded. Further rainfall is likely to occur throughout the week.

Strong Wind Warning for Byron Coast, Coffs Coast and Macquarie Coast October 16 and gale warning was issued for October 17 in Eden Coast and strong wind warning for Byron Coast, Coffs Coast, Macquarie Coast, Hunter Coast, Sydney Coast, Illawarra Coast and Batemans Coast.

Port of San Antonio closes on October 12 due to dense fog Shipping sources on October 13 report that the Port of San Antonio halted operations due to dense fog since 10:45 local time on October 12. It was not immediately indicated when operations would resume.

33 miles SE of Valencia A magnitude 4.0 earthquake struck in the Mediterranean Sea. Incident closed. The European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre reported that a magnitude 4.0 earthquake struck approximately 33 miles southeast of Valencia in the Mediterranean Sea. There were no reports of injuries or major structural damage. This incident is closed.
Strong winds may impact operations at Port of Santos Shipping sources on August 20 indicate that strong winds may cause indirect pilot maneuvers at Port of Santos.

UPDATE: Pier 2 Container Terminal resumed waterside operations Updated sources indicate on January 11 that Pier 2 Container Terminal at the Port of Durban have resumed waterside operations at 22:10 (local time) following disruptions caused by severe winds from January 10-12. Assessment: The developments highlight how efforts to contain COVID-19 have negatively affected supply chains in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). Indeed, commercial shipping operations largely continue throughout region, as, despite many countries having curbed cross-border travel, air, sea, and overland cargo shipments have generally been exempt from such directives. Still, coronavirus-induced restrictions, notably mandatory quarantines, nightly curfews, and enhanced screening procedures, have reduced the capacities of some service providers, delayed cargo handovers and inspections, and extended lead-times, among other issues, leading to incurring storage and demurrage at ports and delays at borders for customs. With some MENA nations having begun to relax such measures, associated disruptions may soon start to dissipate. That said, residual backlogs and service delivery delays should be anticipated.

Mutant Virus Strain May Result in Produce Shortages, Supply Chain Disruptions, Rising Prices in UK On Saturday, December 19, British Prime Minister Boris Johnson announced a new set of restrictive measures due to the emergence of a novel mutant strain of the SARS-CoV-2 virus that causes COVID-19. Preliminary analyses indicate that the strain, which has been dubbed VUI-202012/01, is approximately 70 percent more effectively transmitted from person to person than the existing variant of SARS-CoV-2. The World Health Organization has stated that there is currently no indication that VUI-202012/01 results in more severe COVID-19 than the existing variant of the virus, nor does it possess higher morbidity. As of this writing, there has been no indication that current COVID-19 vaccines are less effective against this variant of the virus. New restrictions imposed across England include shifting areas such as London into Tier 4, wherein residents are to stay at home with the exception of essential activities, and non-essential international travel is banned. Media reports have emerged indicating that additional police units are being deployed to transport hubs such as train stations across the affected areas to enforce compliance with restrictive measures. Furthermore, a number of countries in Europe, including Germany, the Netherlands, France, and Switzerland, as well as elsewhere, have imposed a precautionary ban on travel into their respective territories from the UK for the foreseeable future. While there were no indications of associated bans on travel from mainland Europe into other countries in the region at the time of this writing, it is worth noting that VUI-202012/01 has reportedly also been detected in Denmark, Belgium, and the Netherlands. 



Media reports have emerged indicating that associated restrictions and travel bans are resulting in disruptions to cargo transport, and British ports, which have already been under pressure due to COVID-19 restrictions and a recent uptick in worldwide container traffic, are under increasing strain. Royal Mail has purportedly suspended deliveries of packages and letters from the UK to mainland Europe, and postal services from other countries in the region, such as Germany, to the UK and the Republic of Ireland have likewise been suspended for the foreseeable future. The European Union held a meeting to discuss the bloc’s response to the emergence of VUI-202012/01 on December 21; however, there were no indications as to any conclusions drawn from the meeting known at the time of this writing. 



Assessment: While the novel mutant strain of SARS-CoV-2 is reportedly not associated with higher morbidity, a surge in daily new deaths in the UK is likely in the foreseeable future off the back of rising daily case incidence resultant from higher transmissibility of VUI-202012/01. As the vaccination campaign progresses in the country, community immunization efforts may mitigate the negative impacts of the recent outbreak of this strain. It is worth noting, however, that media reports have emerged suggesting that this strain initially emerged in the UK in September but remained at low levels nationwide until mid-November, when its transmission may have been propagated by an unspecified “super-spreader” event. As such, the possibility that further restrictive measures on movement and/or gatherings may be imposed across England in the coming days and weeks in an effort to curb viral spread cannot be ruled out. 



Tier 4 restrictions and travel bans imposed on the UK by other countries are likely to incur supply chain disruptions to businesses from a variety of sectors, such as manufacturing, due to delays in imports and exports or cancellations of deliveries. Such disruptions are likely to result in financial losses to impacted organizations and, as daily case incidence in the UK is currently on an incremental trajectory, the possibility that these restrictions and associated disruptions may persist for the coming weeks cannot be ruled out. Disruptions to cargo transport may result in shortages of produce, including food, and associated rising prices within the UK for the foreseeable future. It is worth noting, however, that government officials have indicated that only some 19 percent of daily freight traffic is foreseen to be affected by travel bans and other restrictions. It is advised to continue monitoring developments associated with the emergence of VUI-202012/01 in the UK and elsewhere, related restrictions on transit and cargo transport, and heightened police presence across Tier 4 areas. Moreover, it is recommended to be vigilant to the potential for disruptions to supply chains through the UK and possible future shortages of produce in the country.

UPDATE 1 - Agriculture bills increasing intent for opposition unity, COVID-19 disruption will marginally affect public support for Indian government India’s Minister for Food Processing Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned on 17 September after stating that three recently proposed agriculture bills – which have since been passed – would disadvantage farmers, particularly in her representative state of Punjab. Badal is a member of Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), an alliance partner of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led government. Her resignation follows ongoing protests by several hundred thousand farmers in Punjab and neighbouring Haryana against the bills.Farmer protests led by the Indian Youth Congress against the agriculture bills continue in New Delhi, India on 22 September 2020, with thousands participating.Sonu Mehta/Hindustan Times via Getty ImagesProtests from farmers – which are likely to continue over the coming weeks – will probably encourage SAD and other parties to threaten to exit the government alliance, weakening the government’s position in the upper parliamentary house. Minister Badal’s resignation almost certainly came in response to farmers’ opposition to the bills. Although it poses little risk to government continuity, given that further ministerial resignations are unlikely, it is the first major resignation in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s cabinet since he came to power in 2014 and therefore represents an early indication of internal opposition. If farmer protests spread to states such as Bihar and Tamil Nadu – although this is unlikely to happen imminently – SAD and other regional alliance parties are likely to leave the government coalition. In the lower parliamentary house, the BJP holds a simple majority (303 of 542 seats), and although alliance parties strengthen its position, their exit would be unlikely to stall policymaking. In the upper house, the BJP is short of a majority (it holds 86 of 250 seats by itself, and 101 together with allies), and allied parties departing the coalition would strengthen the government’s recent strategy to undertake policymaking via ordinances (a direct executive order), thus bypassing parliament.The government’s preference for policymaking through ordinances will likely encourage attempts by the opposition to unite through co-ordinated policy positions and support for emerging anti-government protests. Since India imposed a national lockdown to mitigate the spread of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) in March, the BJP has undertaken urgent policymaking through ordinances instead – particularly during parliamentary recess. These have included delaying insolvency proceedings, storage of essential commodities, and loan moratoriums. Given that policy will probably stall in the upper house, it is likely that the BJP will continue to use ordinances to pass policy and that the opposition will argue that this subverts parliament. A probable opposition alliance would primarily be led by the main opposition Indian National Congress party and would include parties from states such as Maharashtra and West Bengal, with a focus on negotiating a co-ordinated position against future policies. These policies are very likely to include new labour laws (including legislation designed for contract working and to re-establish mechanisms for workplace audits, which was passed on 23 September), increased privatisation in sectors like banking and mining, and compensation under the Goods and Services Tax. The opposition will also very likely support emerging anti-government protests, including ongoing farmer-led protests and trade union-led strikes against the privatisation programme. Such protests are unlikely to result in policy roll-back, but will probably compel the government to slow implementation. A shift in urban and rural public opinion about the government’s response to COVID-19 – if realised – would indicate a growing likelihood of a cabinet reshuffle, particularly of senior members. India is currently the world’s second-most affected country in terms of the total number of COVID-19 cases and is very likely to overtake the United States, and thus become the epicentre, by November. Anecdotal reporting and IHS Markit sources indicate shifting public perception in key cities such as Mumbai, New Delhi, Chennai, and Bengaluru as healthcare services report a shortage of beds and prolonged response times. Anti-government sentiment appears to be rising, reflected among groups that had hitherto supported the government’s response. This extends to India’s urban upper-middle class, including leaders of medium- to large-sized conglomerates, whose vehicle for protest is unlikely to be street action but will instead take the form of social media rhetoric, coverage in national English-language media, and forthcoming political donations. Their impetus will likely be strengthened by India’s severe economic downturn: the government reported on 31 August that India’s first-quarter fiscal year 2020-21 GDP contracted by 23.9% – the steepest contraction globally this year – and IHS Markit estimates that India’s annual GDP growth will slow to -10.2%. Opposition in India’s non-urban areas – such as in Bihar, where state elections are due by November 2020 – will likely manifest as a reduced vote-share for the BJP. A combination of opposition from India’s upper-middle-class urban population and rural classes will probably force the government to amend its COVID-19 response strategy, and/or pacify such sentiment by undertaking a cabinet reshuffle. Indicators of changing risk environmentIncreasing riskHoarding or sharp price rises for staple foods in response to the reduced government role in setting prices (as stipulated in the new agriculture bills) would likely broaden farmer-led protests to include intermediaries who purchase produce for urban supply.A loss for the BJP in the upcoming Bihar state elections – the first major poll in India since the COVID-19 virus outbreak began – would indicate that public support for the central government is weakening.If the BJP’s parent organisation, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), opposes the agriculture bills and calls for their withdrawal, then this would strongly indicate RSS’s acknowledgement of growing opposition against the government.Decreasing riskThe government announcing a consultation process with farmer groups to reconsider contentious provisions of the agriculture bills would likely limit farmers’ intent for protests at least until after the consultation process.Given opposition parties’ claims of procedural malpractice by the government during the passage of the agriculture bills, guarantees from the government – including a pause on policymaking via ordinances and a revocation of the suspension of some opposition members of parliament – would reduce their intent to form an alliance. CORRECTION: Conditions gradually improve at after court orders Transnet Port Terminals strike halt A previous version of this incident mistakenly classified it as an industrial fire and has now been corrected. 

Reports indicate that a company-wide go-slow strike began at the end of June after the state-owned port operator Transnet Port Terminals failed to disburse an anticipated bonus payment to employees. The strike has resulted in vessel berth waiting times of 4 to 5 days at the Port of Durban, where 60% of South African imports and exports are processed. Unspecified equipment failures are further complicating matters at the port. However, the most severe impacts are at Ngqura Container Terminal near Port Elizabeth, where total waiting times for berths have increased to 7 days or more. At both locations, shipping companies indicated that they are incurring losses of USD 25,000 each day due to the delays, prompting some vessels to bypass ports. Disruptions have also been reported at Port Elizabeth Container Terminal and in Cape Town. Some carriers, such as MSC, Maersk, and ONE have announced the employment of extra loaders in an attempt to minimize delays during port calls in South Africa. 

At Ngqura Container Terminal, container loading has slowed from 25 containers per hour to between 5 and 8 containers per hour. This has had a significant impact on local agricultural cargo, particularly citrus exporters who are in high season between the months of February and August. Citrus industry representatives additionally noted that the go-slow strike has exacerbated pre-existing challenges with low crane capacity, limited cold storage capacity, and limited container availability. 

Volkswagen, one of the container terminal’s largest customers, utilizes the terminal as a critical transit point for parts supplied to their assembly plant in Uitenhage. The plant is missing its production target of 680 units per day by approximately 400 units. Losses are expected to intensify if critical parts for the just-in-time manufacturing process do not arrive soon. A vessel with 150 containers including some critical automotive parts is reportedly in the Nelson Mandela Bay area but has not yet managed to berth at the terminal. Reports indicate that trucks have been forced to wait for up to 18 hours for inbound and outbound shipments, with members of local meat, textile, and electronics industries also reporting ground transportation disruptions.  

Expert testimony to media suggests that the cause of the strike was a critical failure in judgment by Transnet managers. Historically, Transnet has announced incentive bonus payments on the morning that financial statements are released to the public. Such an announcement was anticipated at the end of June and it is understood that employees were under the impression that bonus payments would be processed at that time in a regular fashion. However, the financial statement release has been delayed by an ongoing audit that is not likely to be concluded until mid- August, and Transnet is not able to disburse the funds until the audit is completed. 

As the end of June neared, with funds for bonus payment disbursal inaccessible until the audit is completed, Transnet managers issued a new stipulation that bonus payments will be paid to employees on the condition that employees have met on-time-performance targets, a proposal that was reportedly rejected by some workers. While labor unions representing Transnet employees chose not to resort to industrial action, non-unionized workers expressed frustration at the handling of the matter and organized their own strike. As evidence of their frustration, this action was executed without sanctioning from South African courts, which protects employees from being fired for strike participation.  At least 11 employees have been suspended for their participation. 

On July 14, Transnet announced that it has obtained an interdiction from the Labor Court of Port Elizabeth that orders striking employees to halt their action. Reports on July 15 indicated that performance at Transnet Port Terminals was already improving. Delays are likely to persist as backlogs are cleared.
Customers are advised to monitor further developments on Everstream Analytics.

Greenpeace Protest on Hartman Bridge on Thursday Temporarily Closed Portion of Houston Ship Channel On Thursday, September 12, 23 protesters associated with Greenpeace demonstrated along the Fred Hartman Bridge in Baytown, TX just outside of Houston. The protest began around 6:30 AM local time and included 11 of the protesters rappelling down the bridge to disrupt shipping traffic in the Houston Ship Channel. While the bridge stayed open during the protest to vehicular traffic, a half-mile portion of the ship channel was closed between Light 102A and Light 104 until reopening early Friday morning after protesters were arrested. The protest remained peaceful; however, the initial blocking of the bridge led to a minor motor vehicle accident which injured one person. 

Assessment: The Greenpeace activists stated that their goal of the protest was to attempt to disrupt the oil and gas shipments that go through the Houston Ship Channel. The group timed their protest to attempt to get the attention of Democratic presidential candidates who were in Houston Thursday for a Democrat National Committee presidential debate. The Houston Ship Channel and Port of Houston are vital to U.S. oil and gas exports and the ship channel is the busiest in the country annually generating approximately $339 billion and providing over 1.35 million jobs to the state of Texas. The portion of the ship channel that was closed on Thursday normally sees approximately 300 vessels pass through, and according to media sources, at least seven were blocked during the temporary closure. The protest did not cause any significant disruptions to shipping interests, as many companies often build in an extra day to shipping schedules as a precaution. 

An uptick in climate change-related protests has been seen in recent months, especially across Europe. The majority of protests are organized by groups such as Greenpeace or Extinction Rebellion and have been relatively peaceful, although some have been disruptive with protesters blocking bridges, and trains, similar to the Greenpeace protesters temporarily shutting down the Houston Ship Channel on Thursday. Additionally, a weeklong series of protests are being planned across the world beginning Friday, September 20 as part of a global climate strike action. The relative ease with which the Greenpeace protesters in Baytown were able to shut down a portion of the Houston Ship Channel using a small group of people and the increased focus on climate-related protests highlight the possibility of an increase in similar protests across the United States. As such, Resilience360 customers with cargo interests should anticipate the possibility of disruptions to supply chains due to climate-related protests.

Risks: Protests and riots; labour strikesSectors or assets affected: All sectorsOn 29 August 2018, thousands of members of the United Workers Front (Frente Unitario de Trabajadores (FUT), Ecuador's largest trade union federation held a march in Quito to protest several economic measures adopted by the government through 2018. These include a reduction in gasoline (petrol) subsidies and planned redundancies in the public sector caused by the government's austerity drive that includes a restructuring of ministries, and state-owned enterprises in the public construction, pharmaceutical, and manufacturing sectors. The FUT, alongside other civil society groups representing students, teachers, peasant farmers, and pensioners are planning a national march on 20 September. Separately, the country's largest indigenous umbrella organisation, the Confederation of Indigenous Nationalities of Ecuador, resolved on 29 August to hold a national protest towards the end of October over the same issues. The government is very unlikely to capitulate and reverse these measures; In June public debt reached almost USD48 billion, or 46.1% of GDP. IHS Markit forecasts the fiscal deficit to reach close to 5% of GDP in 2018.Significance: Opposition to the government is likely to mainly take the form of labour strikes, particularly in the public sector, supported by peaceful protest marches involving thousands at a time, towards Quito and other major cities including Cuenca and Guayaquil. Crucially, the 2008 constitution prohibits strikes in strategic sectors including hydrocarbon production and transport, telecommunications, electric energy, health workers, and public transport. Workers in strategic sectors are unlikely to participate in unauthorised work stoppages given the high likelihood of dismissal. The likely convergence of labour, civil society, and indigenous opposition to the government's economic measures would increase the risk of co-ordinated strike action in non-strategic sectors, and also of larger recurring protests capable of causing more significant disruption to commercial activity including roadblocks of major highways in the latter part of 2018. Submission of a legal challenge to the constitutional court to dispute existing restrictions on the right to strike would indicate a rapidly increasing risk of co-ordinated strike action and protests by civil society groups. Over 100 Protesters Detained at Anti-Government Demonstration in Managua on Saturday On Saturday, hundreds of supporters of the Civic Alliance opposition coalition gathered for a demonstration in downtown Managua. The action was intended to protest against the administration of incumbent President Daniel Ortega, and to demand the release of political prisoners. As Ortega s government had previously outlawed anti-government demonstrations, security forces rapidly descended on the scene and forcibly dispersed the crowd with truncheons, tear gas, and rubber bullets. Nicaraguan authorities claimed that 107 protesters were detained for  violating public order.  The opposition claimed that 164 demonstrators were detained, and that six had been wounded by rubber bullets. Multiple news outlets and non-governmental organizations have claimed that several journalists that were covering the demonstration were assaulted by police and/or robbed of their cellphones. There were no reports of injuries among law enforcement personnel. 
	 
	Assessment: Political leaders from the United States, Uruguay, and multiple European countries condemned the actions taken by Nicaraguan authorities on Saturday. Representatives of the European Union called on the Ortega administration to respect the principles of freedom of peaceful assembly and freedom of the press. Nicaragua s opposition movement claims that 770 people have been imprisoned on spurious, politically motivated charges since civil unrest broke out across Nicaragua last April. The government freed 112 detainees in late February, and 50 more were transferred to house arrest on March 15th. 	Assessment: Heavy rains are common across Tanzania during the two rainy seasons, which generally run from March to May and November to December. Assessment: Since the start of the year, there have been 29 piracy incidents reported in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore (SOMS) area. This is a significant increase from the eight incidents that were reported in 2018. While the exact reason for the increase is unknown, it is possible that a new criminal group is operating in the area. The number of incidents is still much lower than the peak of piracy in the region in 2015, which saw 96 incidents. However, the relatively high numbers so far this year could be a sign that piracy is becoming a more serious problem in the SOMS area. Salvage completion on Long Tau River delayed to February 2020 - UPDATE 3 Updated sources indicate that salvage operations of the VietSun Integrity have been temporarily suspended on the Long Tau River due to a major diving incident. The estimated timeline for completion of the operations has been postponed to February 2020. A channel waterway with draft restrictions of 10m has been arranged as an alternative route to Cat Lai Port. Vessels with drafts exceeding 10m have been allowed to pass on a case-by-case basis. 

Previous reporting in October 2019 indicated the following information:  

Cargo vessels with port calls at Cat Lai Container Terminal in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam are facing disruptions in freight movement and restrictions on capacity due to delays in vessel schedules after Long Tau River was closed temporarily on October 19 as a result of a maritime accident. 
VietSun Integrity, a domestic vessel, was carrying 285 unspecified containers with 17 crew members onboard when it started to list and later sank at around 01.30 (local time) on October 19, shortly after leaving the port. Although all crew members were rescued, the containers as well as the ship sank within two hours after the initial distress signal was issued. 

Marine traffic suspended
In response, Ho Chi Minh City Port authorities have temporarily suspended all marine traffic from the junction of the Dong Tranh - Long Tau River for an indefinite period and all vessels to Cat Lai have been directed to use Soai Rạp channel as an alternative route. The closure allows time to clean up 150 tons of spilled oil as well as to recover the lost containers and the ship. 

While initial reports suggested that the closure may last for up to 3 or 4 weeks, local sources on October 30 indicated that it may be extended for up to 100 days or 3 months as the salvage operation is expected to take longer. This is reportedly because the sunken ship may need to be segregated into 20 pieces with a crane. As of October 28, 63 containers have been found, about 42m3 of oil has been collected, and buoys have been placed around the accident site to prevent the oil from spreading further. 

Impact to cargo movement

The average waiting time for vessels at Cat Lai port is currently around 1.5 to 2 days with reports suggesting that marine traffic near the affected site has slowed down. Ships are also facing an increase in fuel costs due to the longer distance that need to be traversed via the Soai Rap River. Moreover, carriers are also being forced to reduce cargo capacity as the river’s depth is shallower than Long Tau River’s. 
At present, the maximum cargo capacity for carriers using the river is at 30 percent with the maximum draft restriction for vessels at 9 meters. Vessels with drafts that are above 9 meters have been directed to Cai Mep International Container Terminal, mainly used for export and import of agricultural products. As the draft restrictions limit vessels in their cargo loading capacity, some shipping lines have reportedly reduced freight at other international ports in order to have enough draft to bypass the route and to pick up goods at Cat Lai Port. As a result, carrier operations and port schedules have been impacted, especially during the peak period of import and export season, as the year is coming to an end. 

The Vietnam Maritime Administration has requested import and export enterprises to provide services at ports in Ho Chi Minh City, Vung Tau, and Dong Nai to ease difficulties for carriers. Cat Lai is the biggest container terminal in Ho Chi Minh City's port area, and is mostly used to ship containers to and from the industrial areas of Ho Chi Minh City. Everstream Analytics customers with shipments to Cat Lai are advised to liaise with local carriers and consider cargo offloading and loading options at Cai Mep - Thi Vai Port to avoid the draft restrictions. However, delays in pickup and delivery services and changes to port calls on short notice can be expected at least until the Long Tau River reopens.

Reports of More than 20 Ships Transporting Australian Coal Waiting for Months to Unload in China According to recent media reports, there are at least 21 ships transporting Australian coal that have been waiting for a month or longer to unload at the Port of Jingtang in Tangshan, southeast of Beijing. Of those anchored off the coast, 15 have been waiting to dock since June. The delays come following reports last month that Chinese authorities had ordered some utilities to stop importing Australian coal. Approximately 400 sailors are onboard the ships off Jingtang, along with up to two million tons of coal. China also officially suspended imports of timber from the Australian state of Victoria this week due to bark beetles having been discovered in previous shipments. A similar ban on timber from Queensland took effect earlier this month.



Assessment: Several of the coal freighters waiting to unload at Jingtang have Indian crew members, and their shipboard conditions have drawn the attention of the Indian government. The Jag Anand, owned by Mumbai-based Great Eastern Shipping, has been waiting to berth since June, with 23 Indian crew aboard, while another ship, the Anastasia, has 18 Indian crew members. The Chinese foreign ministry on Friday denied reports that the Jag Anand has been restricted from departing China, blaming the ship’s operator for not wanting to change its itinerary for financial reasons. Great Eastern Shipping has claimed that it has tried to send the ship on to Japan for a crew change but has been unable to due to unspecified reasons. The crew is unable to disembark in China because of COVID-19 restrictions. The Indian Embassy in China is in contact with the Hebei provincial government over the ship’s situation, and the Australian government has also reached out to Chinese authorities in relation to the ship. According to the International Transport Workers’ Federation (ITF), some of the sailors on the Jag Anand have been on board for nearly two years, while the National Union of Seafarers of India has described the ships waiting off Jingtang as “floating prisons.” There is the potential for labor action in solidarity with the confined sailors, although nothing has been immediately announced. 



The directions last month from Chinese authorities to halt Australian coal imports were reportedly delivered verbally and there has still been no official indication from the government of a direct block on coal from Australia. The Australian government, however, has reported a sharp drop in demand from China for coal over the past month, and some Australian shipments have been diverted to other markets. As for the block on timber shipments due to bark beetles, Australian officials have acknowledged concerns over how effective pest fumigation is on timber from trees that were affected by last season’s wildfires, and have stated that they are cooperating with China on the issue. This would seem to indicate that the ban is a legitimate issue for China to raise, even if it fits nicely with current economic measures being taken against Australia as relations between the two countries remain low. Tensions between Australia and China are likely to deteriorate further as coal shipments remain delayed, while China-India relations could also take another hit if the sailors waiting on the ships become more of a high-profile humanitarian issue. Those with interests that might be impacted by the ongoing frictions in these national relationships are advised to remain abreast of developments.

Tensions with Indigenous Mapuches Remain High in Araucanía after Series of Protests, Arson Attack In recent days, activists affiliated with the Mapuche indigenous community have held a series of demonstrations across the southern region of Araucanía, some of which have degenerated into violent clashes. Last weekend, protesters occupied town halls in the municipalities of Collipulli, Curacautín, Ercilla, Traiguén, and Victoria. Participants alleged that Chilean authorities had failed to comply with Convention C169 of the International Labor Organization (ILO), which holds that indigenous communities should be provided with certain protections. Some demonstrators also called for the release of so-called “political prisoners,” many of whom are members of militant Mapuche groups that have been incarcerated on arson charges. On Sunday, all of the demonstrators at such locations were forcibly evicted, in some cases by crowds of residents with no law enforcement authority. Some news outlets have claimed that unspecified “right-wing groups” instigated violent confrontations. In some cases, vehicles belonging to Mapuche protesters that had been parked nearby were flipped over and/or torched. While there were no reports of any critical injuries, media sources indicate that least 48 people were arrested. 



On Wednesday evening, a band of 15 masked arsonists carried out an attack at a factory in Araucanía’s Padre Las Casas district. At least 14 tractor trailers were set on fire, along with several structures and pieces of heavy machinery.  There were no reports of casualties. A militant Mapuche organization called Weichán Auka Mapu claimed responsibility for the attack. Araucanía Governor Víctor Manoli denounced the incident as an act of terrorism.



Assessment: Multiple factors have contributed to the recent flareup in tensions. First, the lockdown measures that have been implemented throughout the region to help prevent the spread of COVID-19 have brought financial hardship to many members of the Mapuche indigenous community. Araucanía suffered from a relatively high poverty rate (in comparison to the rest of the country) even before the onset of the pandemic. Additionally, a number of incarcerated Mapuche activists have embarked on a hunger strike at prisons in Araucanía and the neighboring region of Bío Bío. They demand that they be permitted to serve the remainder of their sentences under house arrest due to the risks posed by the pandemic. 



In an effort to defuse the situation, Chilean authorities have invited representatives of the Mapuche indigenous community to attend a summit with policymakers on Friday, August 7. While the dialogue process could potentially ease tensions, a number of similar initiatives in the past have either broken down or been boycotted by more radical elements of the indigenous community. The potential for further protest activity and arson attacks will likely remain elevated across southern Chile in the coming weeks. Those with interests in the region are advised to stay abreast of ongoing developments. Furthermore, it is generally advisable to avoid all ongoing protest activity as much as possible, as even demonstrations that are intended to be peaceful can rapidly escalate and turn violent. Additionally, any atypical behavior or suspicious items should be promptly reported to local authorities.

Explosion Targets Oil Tanker at Port of Jeddah, Highlighting Vulnerability to Commercial Shipping No injuries were reported following an explosion that targeted an oil tanker at the Saudi Arabian Port of Jeddah early on Monday, December 14. According to Saudi sources, the British-owned, Singapore-flagged tanker, BW Rhine, was reportedly targeted by a bomb-laden boat at approximately 12:40 AM local time, causing an explosion and a fire. Although the ship’s crew and firefighters reportedly extinguished the fire, the attack caused damage to the tanker’s body, though there are no concerns as of this writing of an oil spill. Reports also indicated that the attack shut down Jeddah port, though as of now, it remains unclear if operations have resumed. The BW Rhine had docked at Jeddah on December 12, carrying over 65,000 tons of gasoline from an Aramco refinery at Yanbu for consumption in the Kingdom. Following the attack, the United Kingdom Marine Trade Operations issued an advisory, stating that an investigation has been opened, and urging all ships in the area to exercise caution. The attack has not yet been claimed by any group. 



Assessment: The incident underscores the vulnerability of Saudi Arabia’s oil infrastructure, and highlights risks posed to commercial shipping in the Red Sea. The explosion also marks the fourth such assault targeting Saudi energy infrastructure in a month. Most recently, a mine exploded off the coast of Shuqaiq and damaged a Maltese-flagged oil tanker on November 25, in an attack claimed by Houthi rebels. Although Saudi officials have not blamed anyone for the most recent attack on December 14, bomb-laden boats and limpet mines have been used periodically by Houthi rebels in the past, suggesting the Shia militia was likely responsible. Saudis typically claim to intercept and destroy unmanned, bomb-laden boats; however, any damage to commercial vessels in this region has the potential to damage production facilities, possibly affecting supply chains and oil prices, as the Red Sea is a vital shipping lane for international energy supplies and other cargo. If attacks successfully damage oil production or result in casualties, this would further increase the risk of conflict in the area. Heightened security is likely at all commercial ports in the Bab al Mandeb Strat in the Red Sea, as well as the Persian Gulf, in the coming days.

Pirates Kidnap Three from Tanker in Gulf of Guinea; Highlighting High Threat from Piracy Earlier this week, sources reported that pirates kidnapped three crewmembers from a tanker in the Gulf of Guinea. Details on the incident remain scarce and disputed; however, the Stelios K tanker reportedly went dark on November 16 either off the coast of Lagos, Nigeria or Lome, Togo. The vessel is believed to have been boarded by pirates who remained onboard until at least November 19. The vessel has since been located and three crewmembers have been reported missing. The Nigerian Navy is searching for the attackers, but no arrests have immediately been reported.



Assessment: The incident brings the total number of kidnappings in the Gulf of Guinea to at 23 so far this year, including 10 in November alone. It also brings the total number of crewmembers kidnapped to nearly 120. While kidnappings remain common in the Gulf of Guinea and are often carried out by piracy groups to secure ransom payments, there have been some suggestions that the latest incident may instead have been related to a business dispute. Regardless, the incident has highlighted the high threat from piracy across the Gulf of Guinea, particularly during the dry season, which generally runs from November to March. Due to the high threat from pirates, all nonessential travel in the Gulf of Guinea should be avoided. Those continuing to operate in the area are urged to exercise a high level of vigilance at all times and ensure that appropriate security measures are in place to deter potential attackers.

Likely collapse of Yemen's Hodeidah ceasefire and government offensive... (FIRST PUBLISHED 19 MARCH 2019)The Houthi movement announced at a news conference in Sanaa on 16 March that its forces would strike Riyadh and Abu Dhabi with ballistic missiles if the implementation of the United Nations (UN)-sponsored peace deal in the port city of Hodeidah was breached. The Houthis claimed to have intelligence that the internationally recognised Yemeni government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia and the UAE, is preparing to resume its offensive on the port city. The Hodeidah ceasefire came into force on 18 December 2018, but there has since been no progress on implementation of a joint withdrawal from the city. Saudi Arabia and the UAE are reportedly now insisting that they are no longer willing to wait.Significance: IHS Markit assesses that the fundamental disagreement between the Houthis and the government over who will provide the 'local forces' to provide security in Hodeidah after a withdrawal is unlikely to be resolved peacefully, and that the UN-sponsored ceasefire is very likely to collapse in the coming weeks. Should this be the case and a government offensive to recapture the city goes ahead, there would be a severe risk of indiscriminate property damage in the city and the adjacent port from Saudi-led coalition airstrikes and shelling, and protracted urban warfare. Faced with the loss of Hodeidah, the Houthi movement would most likely destroy port facilities and deploy sea mines, making the port unusable for at least several months, and resume missile and IED attacks against coalition shipping in the Red Sea. An indicator signalling an imminent government offensive would be an intensification in shelling of Hodeidah's southeastern neighbourhoods. An agreement by both sides to further face-to-face talks on a specific date would at least temporarily reduce the likelihood of a government offensive. In the event of a government offensive, Houthi retaliation would probably also involve the launch of 'Scud'-type missiles and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) strikes at military and infrastructure targets against Saudi Arabia, although their impact would be mitigated by Saudi Patriot air defences. Houthi UAVs are unlikely to have the range to strike targets in the UAE, despite a claimed UAV attack.Risks: Civil war, TerrorismSectors or assets affected: Marine, Ground cargo                    Content provided by IHS Markit Foresight © 2019

Work-to-Rule Labor Action Called at St Petersburg Ford Sollers Factory Facing Shutdown On Friday, a union leader from the Ford Sollers automobile plant in Vsevolzhsk, about ten miles northeast of St Petersburg, announced a work-to-rule strike from the morning of Monday, April 8. The call for labor action short of a full strike was made during a meeting with about 300 workers. Ford is restructuring its operations in Russia and plans to close the St Petersburg site. The work-to-rule plan is intended to apply pressure for renegotiating the terms of planned layoffs, seeking two years  salary for released workers, at least double what Ford is currently offering. A union official claimed production could be heavily slowed if even half of the approximately 900 factory workers strictly function based on the terms of their employment and factory regulations. Pickets and demonstrations are possible during the labor action, union leadership noted, though no specific mobilizations had been immediately announced. 
 
	Assessment: The Ford Sollers plant manufactures the Focus and Mondeo models, and it has experienced similar disruptive labor actions in the past. In 2003, the Ford Focus became the best-selling foreign car model in Russia and held the spot for about a decade before the country s economic crisis heavily dented car sales. Ford is planning to halt passenger vehicle sales in Russia by June of this year while continuing to produce Ford Transit commercial vehicles at a plant in Elabuga managed by Sollers through a joint venture. Though not officially confirmed, the work-to-rule labor action at the Vsevolzhsk facility could be expanded by some workers to a full strike depending on the progress of negotiations. Resilience360 customers are advised to continue monitoring developments and anticipate possible supply chain disruptions due to the planned labor action.

Oil Tanker Reported “Hijacked” in Strait of Hormuz, Reflecting Persistent Risk of Maritime Incidents Reports from July 15 indicated that an oil tanker was hijacked on July 5 off the coast of the United Arab Emirates. It was not immediately clear what happened aboard the Dominica-flagged MT Gulf Sky, as the tanker’s tracker had been turned off around 4:30 AM local time on July 5, though satellite photos showed the vessel in Iranian waters on July 14, off the coast of Hormuz Island. The ship’s captain reported that two of the ship’s sailors are currently in Tehran, while the twenty-six other crew members returned to India. The tanker had previously been positioned near Khor Fakkan, a city on the eastern coast of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), for months, after the US had accused the ship’s Iranian buyers of attempting to purchase the vessel in coordination with the US-sanctioned National Iranian Oil Company, National Iranian Tanker Company, and the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) Quds Force. It remains unclear how the tanker was able to leave the shores of the UAE after being seized by local authorities. No government officials have yet commented on the incident. 



Assessment: The incident stands to aggravate tensions between the US and Iran in the Gulf region. Although Tehran has appeared to scale back incidents of harassment and other provocative activities around the Strait of Hormuz, following an uptick in such incidents last summer, low-level attacks on tankers using limpet mines and incidents of detaining oil vessels have routinely been blamed on Iran. Most recently, a Hong Kong-flagged oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was briefly seized on April 14, allegedly by Iran’s IRGC. Lingering tensions between Washington and Tehran leave open the possibility of further contentious encounters, especially considering that the latest seizure of the MT Gulf Sky represents a possible violation of US sanctions. Tankers in the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, and the Bab al Mandeb Strait continue to be targets as part of Tehran’s efforts to push back against the US, which could potentially result in the indiscriminate detentions of civilian vessels.
